parts.title: My first camping trip
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
Last summer, my school organised a camping trip for our class, and I was terrified. I had never slept outside before, and I am not the kind of person who enjoys insects. My best friend, Daria, was more excited than I was. She had packed a torch, three jumpers and enough biscuits for the whole group.

We arrived at the campsite on a Friday afternoon. The teachers divided us into groups of four, and we had to put up our own tent. It sounded easy, but it took us nearly an hour, because one of the poles was broken and the instructions were missing. When we finally finished, the tent was a little crooked, but it was standing.

That evening we cooked sausages on a fire and told stories. It was the first time I had seen so many stars. I tried to count them, but I gave up after about fifty. Later, at night, the weather changed, and it started to rain heavily. Daria found out that our tent was not completely waterproof when a drop landed on her nose. We moved our sleeping bags to the middle and laughed until morning.

On Saturday we were tired, wet and happy. Our teacher told us that the crooked tent had a prize for being the most creative. I still do not like insects, but I now understand why people enjoy camping. I am already planning to ask my parents if we can go together this summer.

questions.prompt: How did the writer feel before the trip?
questions.explanation: She says she was terrified because she had never slept outside and does not like insects.

questions.prompt: Why did it take so long to put up the tent?
options: They did not know how to start it properly.
They had no teacher to help them at all.
They had left the tent poles at school.
A pole was broken and there were no instructions.
questions.explanation: One of the poles was broken and the instructions were missing, so it took nearly an hour.

questions.prompt: What did the writer enjoy on Friday evening?
questions.explanation: She saw many stars and tried to count them.

questions.prompt: What happened in the night?
questions.explanation: A drop of rain landed on Daria's nose, showing that the tent was not completely waterproof.

questions.prompt: How did the writer feel at the end of the trip?
options: She was too tired to speak.
questions.explanation: She understands why people enjoy camping and wants to ask her parents to go together.

parts.title: A school in the forest
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There are three extra sentences.
parts.passage:
At the edge of a forest in the north of England, a group of children is learning how to light a fire. They are not at school in the usual way, but at a forest school, where children spend most of their lessons outdoors, whatever the weather. [1] Teachers say that this makes children more confident.

A typical day begins with a walk to the clearing, where the group has a base. [2] They use sticks, ropes and old blankets to make a shelter, and in winter they sit round the fire to drink hot chocolate.

The children also learn about nature. They collect leaves, look for insects and listen to the birds. [3] Some of them can now tell the difference between twenty kinds of tree.

Many parents were worried about safety at first. [4] Children learn to use tools carefully, and an adult is always with them. Accidents are rare.

Not every child loves it immediately. [5] "At first, I hated the mud," says nine-year-old Nell. "Now I'd be sad if it was ever sunny."
sentences: Some of them are shy at the start and find the cold and the mud difficult.
However, the forest is not a rough or dangerous place, because the rules are very clear.
The nearest school is more than ten kilometres away.
Rain, wind and snow are all part of the lesson.
First, the children decide what they want to do that day.
Their parents come to watch on Friday afternoons.
Last winter, the whole forest was covered in snow for a month.
After a few months, they know the names of most of the plants around them.

gaps.explanation: "Whatever the weather" leads to rain, wind and snow being part of the lesson; "this" in the next sentence refers to learning outdoors in all weather.
After the walk to the clearing, the children first decide what to do; the next sentence says what they use to build a shelter.
They collect leaves and listen to birds, and after a few months they know the plants; the next sentence says they can name twenty kinds of tree.
Parents were worried about safety, and "However" shows that the forest is not dangerous; the next sentences explain how tools are used carefully.
"Not every child loves it immediately" is followed by the shy children who find the cold and mud difficult, which matches Nell's comment about mud.

parts.title: Staying safe on a hike
parts.instructions: Choose the correct word for each gap.
parts.passage: Going for a long walk in the mountains is a wonderful way to enjoy nature, but you must [1] carefully before you leave. Always check the weather forecast, because conditions can [2] very quickly at high altitude. Wear strong boots and carry a waterproof jacket, even if the sky is blue. You should also take plenty of water and some food, [3] you may feel tired on the way back. It is a good idea to tell someone [4] you are going and when you expect to return. If you get lost, stay where you are, because walking [5] the dark is dangerous, and call for help. Finally, remember to [6] your phone fully charged.

questions.prompt: Gap 1
questions.explanation: You must "plan carefully" before a hike.

questions.prompt: Gap 2
questions.explanation: Mountain weather can "change" quickly.

questions.prompt: Gap 3
questions.explanation: "Because" gives the reason for taking food and water: you may feel tired.

questions.prompt: Gap 4
questions.explanation: You tell someone "where you are going".

questions.prompt: Gap 5
questions.explanation: The fixed expression is "in the dark".

questions.prompt: Gap 6
questions.explanation: You "keep" a phone charged; the other verbs do not fit with "fully charged".

parts.title: Getting ready for camping
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage:
Hi Wyn,
I am so excited about our camping trip on Saturday! I have already packed my sleeping bag, [1] I still need to buy a new torch. My brother says we should take warm clothes, [2] it can get very cold at night, even in summer. Do you know [3] to put up the tent? If not, I will show you. We are going to cook sausages on a small stove, so do not forget to bring a plate [4] a fork. I [5] never been to this campsite, but I have heard that it is next to a lake. I hope the weather stays dry [6] the whole weekend!
Pieter

gaps.explanation: "But" contrasts what he has done with what he still needs to do.
"Because" gives the reason for taking warm clothes.
"Do you know how to put up the tent?" asks about the method.
"And" joins the plate and the fork.
The present perfect "have never been" talks about his experience.
"For the whole weekend" says how long.

parts.title: Short conversations
parts.instructions: Listen to seven short conversations. Choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: ambrose
turns.text: Good morning, campers. This is a message about the bus to Blue Lake. The timetable on your programme says that the bus leaves at nine o’clock, but that’s last year’s information, so please ignore it. Because of roadworks on the main road, the driver will leave at ten past nine, and he will not wait for anybody. If you miss it, the next one goes at ten o’clock, but it’s already full with the school group. So please be at the gate five minutes before, with your bag and your lunch. Thank you.

question.explanation: The programme says nine and the next bus at ten is full, but the correct departure is ten past nine because of the roadworks.

turns.speaker: ulrika
turns.text: Hello, Mrs Clark, this is Ulrika from Pine Valley Camp. Don’t worry, Basil is fine and he’s having a great time. He asked me to call because he’s a little embarrassed. He brought his torch, and I checked his water bottle this morning, it’s full. But when he opened his bag tonight, he realised he’d left his sleeping bag on the sofa at home. We have a spare one for tonight, so he won’t be cold. Could you send his own tomorrow, with the bus. He will be very grateful. Thank you very much, and have a good evening.

question.explanation: The torch and the water bottle are in his bag, but he left the sleeping bag at home, and she asks the mother to send it.

turns.speaker: ezekiel
turns.text: Henrike, we need to decide which way we’re going to walk back to the camp.

turns.speaker: henrike
turns.text: I’d like to go over the hill. The view is great from the top.

turns.speaker: ezekiel
turns.text: Yes, but it’s a very steep climb, and you’re already tired. The route along the lake is flat, but it’s twice as long, and we’d be back after dark.

turns.speaker: henrike
turns.text: True. What else is there?

turns.speaker: ezekiel
turns.text: The path through the woods is shaded and short. It joins the main road after twenty minutes. We’ll be there for dinner.

turns.speaker: henrike
turns.text: Fine, let’s do that.

question.explanation: The hill is steep and the lake route is long, so they choose the short, shaded path between the trees.

turns.speaker: percival
turns.text: Welcome to Oak Hill campsite. How many nights are you staying?

turns.speaker: arabella
turns.text: Two nights, please, for one tent. I thought about staying three, but I have to be back at work on Monday.

turns.speaker: percival
turns.text: No problem. It’s twelve pounds a night for each tent. A third night would have made it thirty-six, so you save some money this way.

turns.speaker: arabella
turns.text: And is there a charge for the shower?

turns.speaker: percival
turns.text: No, it’s free. So that’s the total for the weekend, please.

turns.speaker: arabella
turns.text: Here you are. Thank you.

question.prompt: How much will the woman pay?
question.explanation: Twelve pounds is the price per night and thirty-six would be three nights, but she stays two, so she pays twice twelve.

turns.speaker: mortimer
turns.text: Hi Seraphina, it’s Mortimer. About the walk on Saturday, I’ve been thinking. This evening is out, because the forecast is for heavy rain, and I don’t want to be in the dark on a muddy path. Tomorrow afternoon would be nice, but I’ve got a dentist appointment at two, and I’ll be late. So what about going first thing, say nine o’clock, before it gets warm. I’ll bring the coffee if you bring the sandwiches, and we can eat at the top. Call me back, please, and tell me what you think.

question.prompt: When will they go for a walk?
question.explanation: This evening will have heavy rain and he has an appointment tomorrow afternoon, so he suggests the early hour of the next day.

turns.speaker: evangeline
turns.text: Hector, I think we should put the tent near the river. It’s flat and pretty.

turns.speaker: hector
turns.text: I don’t know. The toilets are far from there, but that doesn’t bother me. And the water is a bit noisy, but that would help me sleep, not keep me awake. The problem is the sky. Look at those clouds.

turns.speaker: evangeline
turns.text: It might not rain.

turns.speaker: hector
turns.text: Last year a man at the campsite told me that the river can rise very quickly in a storm. He had to run to higher ground in the middle of the night.

turns.speaker: evangeline
turns.text: Oh dear. Let’s go up there, near the trees.

question.prompt: Why don't they put the tent near the river?
options: It is too far from the toilets.
question.explanation: The toilets and the noise do not worry him; it is the sky, because the river can rise quickly in a storm.

turns.speaker: lazarus
turns.text: What are we eating tonight, Odessa? I’m starving.

turns.speaker: odessa_x
turns.text: I was going to cook sausages, but we finished them for lunch yesterday, and the shop is too far. I also thought about heating some soup, though it takes ages on this little stove.

turns.speaker: lazarus
turns.text: Hmm. And I’m tired of soup.

turns.speaker: odessa_x
turns.text: So I bought some pasta in the village, the long Italian kind, with a jar of tomato sauce. It takes ten minutes, and there’s enough for both of us, even for seconds.

turns.speaker: lazarus
turns.text: Perfect. Let me get the pan, and I’ll wash the plates afterwards.

turns.speaker: odessa_x
turns.text: Deal. You’re a good friend.

question.explanation: The sausages are finished and soup is too slow, so she will cook the long Italian noodles with sauce, which is pasta.

parts.title: Understanding the main idea
parts.instructions: Listen to six short conversations and choose the best answer.

turns.speaker: dominic
turns.text: Rowena, I don’t understand. We’ve been walking for two hours, and I haven’t seen the lake yet.

turns.speaker: rowena
turns.text: Have you got your map? Are you tired? Is your leg hurting from yesterday?

turns.speaker: dominic
turns.text: My leg is fine, and we still have plenty of sandwiches. But I think we took the wrong path at the stream. That sign said Hilltop, not Lakeside.

turns.speaker: rowena
turns.text: Oh no. We should go back, shouldn’t we?

turns.speaker: dominic
turns.text: Yes, I’m sure it was a mistake. It will take an extra hour, and we have to hurry before it gets dark.

options: He has run out of food.
He has taken a wrong turn.
question.explanation: His leg is fine and there are sandwiches; he is lost because he followed the Hilltop sign instead of Lakeside.

turns.speaker: tatiana
turns.text: Magnus, I didn’t sleep at all. Did you hear them last night?

turns.speaker: magnus
turns.text: The group at the next tent? Yes, they were singing till three o’clock.

turns.speaker: tatiana
turns.text: And shouting. I’m cross. I’m going to talk to the manager.

turns.speaker: magnus
turns.text: Fair enough. At least our tent stayed dry, and the toilets were clean this morning.

turns.speaker: tatiana
turns.text: That’s something, I suppose. But I came here for peace and quiet, and it was like a party. I want them to stop tonight.

turns.speaker: magnus
turns.text: I’ll come with you, so he understands that it’s a serious problem for both of us.

options: A group is making a noise.
question.explanation: The tent is dry and the toilets are clean; she is angry because the neighbours sang and shouted until three o’clock.

turns.speaker: cassius
turns.text: I’d like some walking boots for a camping trip in October. These are nice and soft, aren’t they?

turns.speaker: priscilla
turns.text: They are the most comfortable in the shop, but they aren’t waterproof. In autumn the ground is wet and your feet will be soaked.

turns.speaker: cassius
turns.text: Hmm. What about this cheaper pair?

turns.speaker: priscilla
turns.text: The price is better, but they leak at the sides. If I were you, I’d pay a bit more and buy the ones that keep out water. You’ll be glad on the first rainy day.

turns.speaker: cassius
turns.text: You’ve convinced me. Can I try the pair with the red laces?

question.prompt: What does the shop assistant recommend?
question.explanation: The soft pair is not waterproof and the cheap pair leaks, so she advises him to buy the ones that keep out the rain.

turns.speaker: olivier
turns.text: Annelise, are you sure you want to camp again? Putting up the tent takes forever.

turns.speaker: annelise
turns.text: It’s not that bad, it takes twenty minutes if we work together. And cooking outside is part of the fun.

turns.speaker: olivier
turns.text: But hotels have beds and hot water. I think I prefer them.

turns.speaker: annelise
turns.text: They cost a fortune in the summer, true, but that’s not the point. In a hotel you don’t hear the owls or see the stars. I wake up feeling happier after a night in a tent.

turns.speaker: olivier
turns.text: Okay, you win. Let’s book the campsite.

question.prompt: What does the woman think about camping?
options: It is better than a hotel.
question.explanation: The work is not a problem and she does not say it is too expensive; she prefers the owls, the stars and waking up happier, so it is better than a hotel.

turns.speaker: serafina
turns.text: You’ve been scratching your arm all morning, Cyrus. What’s wrong?

turns.speaker: cyrus_x
turns.text: I think I caught a cold in the night. It was freezing in the tent, and my arm feels strange.

turns.speaker: serafina
turns.text: A cold doesn’t make your arm itch. Show me. Look, there’s a small red spot with a hard centre.

turns.speaker: cyrus_x
turns.text: Maybe I fell on the wet grass yesterday, when we were running.

turns.speaker: serafina
turns.text: That would make you dirty, not itchy. I’m sure it’s a bite from some insect that came into the tent. Put some cream on it.

turns.speaker: cyrus_x
turns.text: Thanks. I’ll ask the leader.

question.prompt: What does Serafina think happened to Cyrus?
options: An insect bit him in the night.
He fell over on the wet grass.
He caught a cold during the night.
question.explanation: A cold does not make the arm itch and a fall would make him dirty; the red spot with a hard centre tells her it is a bite.

turns.speaker: gideon_x
turns.text: Good afternoon. Are you staying in the forest campsite tonight?

turns.speaker: thomasina
turns.text: Yes. Is the path to the top still open? We want to see the sunrise.

turns.speaker: gideon_x
turns.text: It’s open, and the weather will be dry until Thursday. I’d like to warn you about something else. The grass is very dry after the hot summer, so a small spark can start a big fire.

turns.speaker: thomasina
turns.text: Oh. We were going to cook on a campfire.

turns.speaker: gideon_x
turns.text: Please use a stove instead. It’s safer for you and for the trees.

turns.speaker: thomasina
turns.text: Of course, we’ll do that.

question.prompt: What is the ranger worried about?
question.explanation: The path is open and the weather is dry, but the grass is so dry that a spark could cause a fire, so he asks them to use a stove.

parts.title: A guide talks about a nature walk
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note. Write one or two words, a number, a date or a time.

turns.speaker: speaker-1
turns.text: Good morning, and welcome to Lake Meadow Nature Park. My name’s Marietta, and I’ll be your guide today. We’re going to follow the Heron Trail, which is named after the large grey birds that fish in the shallow water. You may remember that there’s another path called the Otter Trail, which is shorter, but it’s closed at the moment because of building work. Our trail is about six kilometres long. Some people say it’s eight, but that includes the way back to the car park, and we’ll take the shuttle bus for that. We begin at the visitor centre, just behind me. Please don’t go to the cafe yet; you can have a coffee when we finish. The first part of the path goes through an old wood. If you look up, you might see squirrels in the trees. Many visitors hope to see a deer, but they’re shy and usually hide, so don’t be sad if you don’t. In the middle of the walk, we’ll stop for a picnic by the water. After that, the path climbs slowly to a small hill, where there’s a lovely view. The whole walk takes about three hours, with the stops. I know the leaflet says two and a half, but that is for fast walkers, and we aren’t in a hurry. Before we start, a word about clothes. It has rained all week, so the park is very green, but also very muddy. The ground can be wet and rocky, so please wear strong shoes. Sandals are not suitable, and umbrellas are a nuisance among the branches. Please stay close to me and keep to the path, because the edge of the water is soft. Don’t pick the flowers and take your rubbish with you. If you have any questions, ask me at any time. Right, let’s go!

gaps.prompt: The route is named after a large grey bird: the ___ Trail
gaps.explanation: It is named after the heron; the Otter Trail is closed.

gaps.prompt: Distance of the walk, not counting the bus ride: ___ kilometres
gaps.explanation: The trail is six kilometres, not eight; the extra is the way back.

gaps.prompt: The group meets at the ___ near the car park
gaps.explanation: They start at the visitor centre, not the cafe.

gaps.prompt: In the woods, walkers may spot small animals called ___
gaps.explanation: Squirrels are possible; deer are shy and hide.

gaps.prompt: With the stops, the walk lasts about ___ hours
gaps.explanation: It takes three hours; the leaflet’s two and a half is for fast walkers.

gaps.prompt: For the wet and rocky ground, walkers need to wear strong ___
gaps.explanation: The guide asks for strong shoes; sandals are not suitable.

parts.title: An interview with a mountain guide
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Rosalba, you’ve been a mountain guide for fifteen years. What do you like most about it?

turns.speaker: rosalba
turns.text: Photographs are nice, but I take very few, honestly. And I’m not alone in the mountains, because I’m always with a group, so the quiet isn’t what I like. For me, the best moment is when a tired person arrives at the top and realises they’ve done it. I see the smile on their face, and I think, this is why I do this job.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What should people bring?

turns.speaker: rosalba
turns.text: Ropes are only for glaciers and dangerous places, so beginners almost never need one. A camera would be nice, but it’s not really necessary. What you really have to carry is a good pair of boots, soft inside and strong outside. If your feet hurt, you can’t enjoy anything, however good the view is.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What mistakes do beginners make?

turns.speaker: rosalba
turns.text: They almost always do what the guide says, which is great. They don’t usually pack too much food either, we have a rule about that. The mistake is the speed. They are so excited that they start fast, and after one hour they have no energy left. I keep saying, slowly, slowly, you have all day.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: I understand you were once caught in a storm.

turns.speaker: rosalba
turns.text: Yes, six years ago, with eight clients. It was terrifying. The wind knocked one of the clients over, and we could not see ten metres. After that I thought about taking only small groups, but it wouldn’t have changed anything. I also considered cancelling afternoon trips, but storms can come at any hour. The real lesson was to have enough food and warm clothes in the bag at all times, even when it’s sunny. We were cold, but we were safe because of that.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Are the mountains changing?

turns.speaker: rosalba
turns.text: The paths have always been steep, that’s the nature of mountains. The weather is warmer, yes, and it concerns me, but I’d say something else bothers me more. People leave bottles, bags and wrappers along the paths. I spend half of my days collecting rubbish, and it makes me angry. Last month we filled forty bags in a single weekend.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Finally, what would you say to a beginner?

turns.speaker: rosalba
turns.text: Don’t join a club in another country, and don’t spend a fortune on equipment you’ll never use. Just start with short walks near your house, on Sundays. Get used to the feeling of walking for hours, and then you can think about the bigger mountains.

questions.prompt: What does Rosalba like most about her job?
options: Working alone in a quiet place
questions.explanation: She takes few photographs and is never alone; the best moment is when a tired person arrives at the top and smiles.

questions.prompt: What is the most important thing to bring, according to Rosalba?
questions.explanation: Ropes are for glaciers and cameras are not necessary; what you need is a good pair of boots.

questions.prompt: What mistake do beginners usually make?
options: They do not listen to the guide.
questions.explanation: They listen to the guide and do not pack too much; the problem is that they start fast and run out of energy.

questions.prompt: What did Rosalba learn from the storm?
options: To cancel trips in the afternoon
To carry food and warm clothes
questions.explanation: Smaller groups and fewer afternoon trips would not have changed anything; the lesson was to carry food and warm clothes.

questions.prompt: What problem does she mention about the mountains today?
options: There is rubbish on the paths.
questions.explanation: Paths have always been steep and the warmer weather concerns her, but what bothers her more is rubbish left on the paths.

questions.prompt: What advice does she give to beginners?
options: Start with short walks near home
Join a mountain club in another country
Buy lots of expensive new equipment
questions.explanation: She says do not join a club abroad or buy expensive equipment; start with short walks near your house.
